messages:
julia: Kicking off ATL1 warmup smoke now. Goal: validate GPU pools, network fabric (RDMA/MTU), control-plane reachability, and basic SLO gates before handing to platform oncall. I pasted the quick checklist below — please run checks and reply inline with PASS/FAIL + short notes. @cheng you own GPU health, @samir you own networking. ops-bot will post cluster health after each step.

cheng: On it. I'll start nvml + driver checks on gpu-subclusters.

ops-bot: Automated check triggered: `cluster-atl1` preflight start. Running node_agent, service_discovery, and quota sanity. ETA ~3m.

samir: Starting RDMA/mtu sweep. Will run iperf and check hostdev passthrough on the first two nodes.

julia: Checklist (short):
1) Control plane TLS + API reachability (`kubectl get nodes`)
2) Node GPU driver & nvml health (`nvidia-smi -q`)
3) Inference runtime smoke: deploy small model pod, run single-request latency test
4) KV cache warmup check (prefix caching) — smoke script
5) Network fabric: MTU, RDMA, cross-AZ latency, egress routes + NAT throughput
6) Autoscaler sanity: scale-up/scale-down with synthetic load
7) Cost throttle sanity: confirm cost-limits/policy enforced on burst pools
8) SLO gates: 99th p50/p95 token latency and error rate under baseline load
9) Logs/tracing: sample trace end-to-end for a streaming request
10) Handoff signoff: all PASS or open items tracked in ticket

leah: Quick note: For (3) use `runtest/infer_smoke.py --model tiny-llm --qps 1 --tokens 64` to keep cheap.

devops-jordan: Also run `kubectl describe pod <smoke-pod>` if the pod doesn't transition. Saw a taint issue last time.

cheng: GPU driver/pass: PASS. `nvidia-smi -q` shows all devices present, ECC disabled (expected), temp nominal. One node had stale cuda 11.4 symlink; I fixed it. Logs: `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` had no errors.

ops-bot: GPU health aggregated: 24/24 GPUs healthy, nvml ok, driver versions consistent.

samir: Network MTU/rdma: FAIL on node atl1-azb-03 — hostdev didn't bind VF. iperf shows 110Gb/s on healthy hosts, failing host at 0.8Gb/s. I'm re-provisioning SR-IOV config now.

julia: Thanks. samir, please file a prep ticket for that node and mark it OOS for now. We need 2/3 healthy AZs to proceed.

samir: Filed ticket INFRA-6123, node marked OOS. Reprovision started.

leah: Inference runtime smoke: deployed tiny-llm pod, ran `runtest` script. Latency observed: p50 32ms, p95 220ms, 99th 480ms under qps=1. Error rate 0%. PASS unless we want tighter p95.

devops-jordan: Autoscaler test: simulated spike to 200 qps. Observed scale-up from 4->12 nodes in ~45s. Scale-down cooldown respected. PASS. Logged the exact timeline to the runbook.

julia: KV cache warmup: ran `cache_warm.sh` and then measured token cost delta. Cache hit rate ~68% after warmup — matches expectation for small model. PASS.

ops-bot: Tracing sample posted: https://console/redwood/traces/atl1/trace-0x9f... (automated)

leah: End-to-end streaming test: saw a reconnect at 1 attempt on a single session (client-side socket timeout). Root cause seems to be kube-proxy restarts on that node earlier. Marking as INFO not blocker.

julia: SLO gate check: baseline load p95 target = 300ms. Current p95 = 220ms -> PASS. 99th = 480ms which is above soft target 400ms — flagging as regression risk. ops team, advise on mitigation (quantization, smaller batch sizes) before full handoff.

samir: Node reprovision fixed VF binding. Re-ran iperf: 110Gb/s. Node back in pool.

cheng: After node reinstated, GPU heatmap looks normal. No memory leaks reported. PASS.

julia: Cost controls: verified burst-pool throttle rules active; synthetic load didn't consume more than reserved commit. We should still annotate cost projection in the ticket.

devops-jordan: Quick command snippets I used:
```
# smoke pod deploy
kubectl apply -f manifests/smoke/tiny-infer.yaml
kubectl logs -f deploy/tiny-infer -c runner
# run runtime test
python runtest/infer_smoke.py --model tiny-llm --qps 1 --tokens 64
```

oncall-bot: Handoff checklist automated: steps 1-6 PASS, step 5 (network) had transient FAIL but resolved, step 8 (SLO 99th) WARNING. Opening handoff ticket: HANDOFF-ATL1-2024. Please attach outstanding mitigation plan.

julia: Decision: Proceed to limited platform handoff but mark as a partial handoff (canary tenant only). Need mitigation plan for 99th percentile latency (e.g., enable 8-bit quantization for canary, reduce batch window to 8ms). Assigning action items: @cheng tune runtime quantization configs, @leah run canary with 10 tenants, @samir monitor RDMA for 24h.

cheng: Will prepare quantization/knobs diff and link to PR. ETA 3h.

leah: Canary run scheduled in 30m. I'll post metrics.

samir: Monitoring thresholds set, RDMA alerts enabled.

julia: Great work team. I'll update the master ticket with PASS/OPEN items and schedule the readiness review with platform at 14:00 UTC. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Automated check complete: cluster `atl1` warmup status = PARTIAL_HANDOFF. Details -> https://infra/redwood/atl1/warmup/1732104567

samir: FYI cost projection for 24h (based on current utilization): ~$3,200/day for the burst-enabled config. Filed cost note in HANDOFF-ATL1-2024.

leah: Canary initial metrics posted: 10 tenants, p95 240ms, 99th 350ms, error 0. Canary looks stable.

julia: Closing thread for now — all action items tracked. Anyone with objections ping me offline.
